name: Agriculture
title: Field operations planning assistant
summary: Combine field observations, weather, equipment, and agronomist-approved practices into reviewable farm work plans.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A grower cooperative coordinates irrigation inspections and field work across farms with uneven sensor coverage. Satellite imagery, soil readings, weather forecasts, and operator observations arrive at different resolutions. The system prepares field-specific evidence and scheduling options while agronomists and farm managers make crop and application decisions.
problem: A coarse weather forecast or ambiguous image cannot establish conditions in every field. Unit mistakes, boundary errors, and stale sensor readings can turn a reasonable summary into an unsuitable work recommendation, particularly when farms share machinery and water access.
whyAgents: Observation, weather, resource, and practice-retrieval specialists keep uncertain evidence separate. A scheduling engine applies manager-approved constraints; the agents explain missing information and propose inspections before high-consequence actions.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure useful inspections and planning effort before claiming changes in yield or resource use. Agronomic outcomes depend on local conditions and professional decisions, so retain those contextual variables when evaluating the workflow.

agents.name: Field evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Associate sensor readings and imagery with governed field boundaries and capture dates.
agents.boundary: Cannot diagnose crop disease or infer unobserved field conditions as facts.

agents.name: Weather window analyst
agents.responsibility: Compare forecast intervals with approved field-work constraints.
agents.boundary: Cannot guarantee rainfall or waive safe operating restrictions.

agents.name: Equipment planner
agents.responsibility: Match available machinery, operator skills, and access windows to proposed tasks.
agents.boundary: Cannot dispatch equipment or control autonomous machinery.

agents.name: Agronomy briefing agent
agents.responsibility: Retrieve locally approved practices and compile questions for agronomists.
agents.boundary: Cannot prescribe chemical applications, dosing, or treatment decisions.

systems.name: Farm management platform
systems.role: Owns field identifiers, crop records, manager assignments, and accepted work tasks.

systems.name: Geospatial and sensor systems
systems.role: Provide observation footprints, units, timestamps, and data quality metadata.

systems.name: Equipment and water scheduling systems
systems.role: Supply resource availability and approved operating constraints through scoped adapters.

flow.title: Register field concern
flow.description: Bind the observation to a farm and field polygon, retaining source resolution and any boundary uncertainty.

flow.title: Check observation quality
flow.description: Validate sensor units, calibration status, and capture time; label missing coverage rather than interpolating hidden certainty.

flow.title: Gather local context
flow.description: Retrieve crop stage, prior field work, access constraints, and agronomist-approved practices relevant to the task.

flow.title: Evaluate work windows
flow.description: Compare weather revisions, equipment availability, and shared resource constraints using declared planning assumptions.

flow.title: Review proposed inspection
flow.description: Present managers and agronomists with evidence, uncertainty, and a bounded task proposal before any operational commitment.

flow.title: Record approved work
flow.description: Publish the accepted task through the farm platform and capture operator observations to confirm or reject the original concern.

diagrams.caption: A soil probe reports in a different unit than expected. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A soil probe reports in a different unit than expected.
failures.detection: Schema validation detects a unit mismatch or impossible value range.
failures.recovery: Reject the reading until the sensor mapping is corrected and show the field as lacking reliable measurement.

failures.scenario: A field polygon overlaps a neighboring farm.
failures.detection: Boundary registry and observation footprint checks disagree on ownership.
failures.recovery: Restrict retrieval and task generation until the responsible manager confirms the correct parcel boundary.

controls: Validate geospatial ownership and farm access before exposing field-level observations.
Attach units, capture time, and spatial resolution to every sensor or imagery claim.
Keep agronomic prescriptions and chemical application decisions with qualified local professionals.
Require manager approval before dispatching machinery or reserving shared resources.
Expire weather-dependent plans and recheck conditions before field execution.

metrics.name: Observation usability
metrics.definition: Field concerns with sufficient validated local evidence divided by concerns evaluated.

metrics.name: Planning preparation time
metrics.definition: Elapsed time from accepted concern to manager-reviewable inspection or work options.

metrics.name: Spatial attribution accuracy
metrics.definition: Audited observations assigned to the correct field divided by audited observations.

metrics.name: Plan expiry rate
metrics.definition: Approved tasks requiring revalidation because weather or access assumptions changed divided by approved tasks.

tradeoffs.benefit: Combines broad imagery with local measurements.
tradeoffs.cost: Different spatial resolutions can create misleading precision.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces conflicting equipment and water plans.
tradeoffs.cost: Requires timely availability updates from independent farms.

tradeoffs.benefit: Limits action based on uncertain observations.
tradeoffs.cost: Some decisions wait for field staff or agronomist availability.

rollout.acceptance: Managers validate units, boundaries, missing coverage, and uncertain weather using known scenarios.
A bounded crop and region assess task usefulness without equipment control or application recommendations.
Shared-resource reservations begin only after weather-expiry and cross-farm access tests pass.
